meta.subject: Maths
meta.title: Place Value & Expanded Form — 7-Digit Numbers
meta.subtitle: Number discs + place-value charts (up to millions)

items.text: Students will write 7-digit numbers in expanded form using number discs and place-value charts.

note.title: Misconception alert — missing zeros
note.body: Students often miss zeros in expanded form (e.g. writing 20,000 instead of 200,000) because they lose track of the place-value columns. Correction: “Look at our drawing — it shows 2 discs in the Hundred Thousands column, and each disc is worth 100,000, making it 200,000.”

sections.greeting: Today we learn to break 7-digit numbers into expanded form using number discs — so we can read large amounts, like the cost of building a new hospital in our city.

stories.label: Recall
stories.text: Remember the base-ten blocks from yesterday? How can we show that as a simple drawing today? — We can draw circles or dots inside a place-value chart.

stories.label: Try it
stories.text: Imagine Ali has 3,000,000 Rupees. In the air, draw the discs for this number in the Millions column. Ready? Go!

sections.title: The board — 5,234,678 as discs + expanded form

steps.label: Look (45s)
steps.body: Give students 45 seconds to study the chart and think about what it represents.

steps.label: Count each column
steps.body: With Bunty, count the discs column by column: Millions → 5,000,000; Hundred Thousands → + 200,000; Ten Thousands → + 30,000; Thousands → + 4,000; and so on — each disc translates to the number with exactly the right zeros.

steps.label: Combine
steps.body: Add all the expanded parts together to get the standard form: 5,234,678.

cfu.q: Which part of the drawing shows 200,000?
cfu.a: The 2 discs in the Hundred Thousands column.

cfu.q: If Bunty adds one more disc to the Thousands column, what does that column become?
How does drawing discs help avoid missing zeros?
cfu.a: You read the exact place-value heading, so you know how many zeros belong to that column.

sections.task: In pairs, one student is the “drawer” and the other the “writer”. The drawer draws the number discs for 6,781,234 in a place-value chart; the writer writes the expanded-form equation underneath. Then switch roles for 3,210,456.
sections.note: Individual (Page 6): imagine counting bricks to build a new school in Lahore — draw the discs and write 7,654,321 in expanded form.

differentiation.struggling: Provide a pre-drawn 7-column place-value chart for students to draw their discs into.
differentiation.advanced: Write a number greater than 7,654,321 and prove it by drawing the discs for the Millions and Hundred Thousands columns.

afl.instruction: Thumbs up for True, thumbs down for False.

items.text: 3 discs in the Hundred Thousands column equals 30,000.
Expanded form helps us see the value of each digit in a big number.
If I have 0 discs in the Tens column, I write nothing for the Tens place in my standard number.

sections.exitTicket: Ask: Where else in your neighbourhood do you see numbers like this? (property prices, bank boards, population signs).
